customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned as ARG in the Dockerfile. Renovate's built-in dockerfile manager only reads FROM lines, so the '# renovate:' annotations above each ARG are invisible without this.
Commits pinned as ARG in the Dockerfile. oh-my-zsh ships no tags, so there is no version to track - git-refs watches the named branch and bumps the digest.

packageRules.description: One grouped PR a week for the image toolchain rather than a PR per release - claude-code alone ships most days. Typed build, not chore: these bumps change what is inside the published image, so they belong in the changelog and should cut a release. config:recommended's :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers types everything here chore, which release-please hides.
Patch and minor bumps land unattended once the image builds and every binary still runs. Majors always wait for a human.
herdr is pre-1.0 and ships weekly, so a 0.x minor is a breaking change in practice - the one bump worth eyeballing.
Action digests, grouped and scheduled like the image toolchain. Eleven actions arriving as eleven unscheduled PRs is how a pinning policy stops being read.

No automerge for actions. A digest that moved underneath a tag is the supply-chain event hash-pinning exists to surface - merging it unread is the one update type where automerge defeats its own purpose.

docker:// steps are depType docker, which helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests skips - it pins only action and workflow. Digest them too, as tag@sha256 so the version stays readable; actionlint and zizmor both accept that form, and it clears zizmor's unpinned-images audit.
The one-shot pin is not a routine bump and should not wait for the weekly window - until it lands, CI's unpinned-uses gate has nothing to pass against.
